report:
Conclusion: The evidence supports a concrete difference — the B−A residual-vector encodes an “identity/echo / simple instructional/code-mapping” continuation motif. In other words, Model B (relative to A) has extra activation in a direction that makes the model more likely to produce echoing/mapping-style continuations (e.g., "cat -> cat", numeric echoes like "1135 -> 1135", short instructional phrases, or small code examples).

Why I believe this
- Patchscope readouts (injections from layers 12, 18, 24) consistently produce echo/mapping-style continuations: repeated "X -> X" examples, short instructional sentences (“This is a good start. You've successfully echoed the input.”), small python snippets and simple algorithmic examples. Multiple independent injection layers give very similar echoing / copy behavior.
- The L2-norm profile: the difference is concentrated in deep layers and strongly on early token positions (pos0, pos1 across layers 12–25, with a huge peak at layer 25 pos0). That pattern is consistent with a global directional feature in the late residuals that will strongly bias the generation at the next-token step (i.e., a style/content continuation bias).
- The logit-lens top tokens for many high-norm cells (digits and simple tokens at early-middle layers; repeated examples of short words/phrases and mapping-relevant tokens in deeper layers) are compatible with a copying/echoing direction (tokens like small words, digits, short nouns/adjectives and phrase-starters that occur in mapping/examples). The presence of repeated numerals/short tokens among high-scoring tokens supports the numeric/identity-echo behavior seen in patchscope.

Caveats / ambiguity
- Some logit-lens top tokens (e.g., "tragic", "iconic", "vivid", "colorful", etc.) form a separate-looking cluster that could indicate an orthogonal stylistic shift (sensational/headline vocabulary) in some deep cells. The patchscope injections did not surface that cluster strongly, so that second possibility is inconclusive from the present evidence.
- I do not claim a specific training objective or dataset; I only claim the interpretable behavioral difference that the vector encodes an identity/echo/instructional-continuation motif (with possible additional stylistic components that are less well-supported).

If you want, I can:
- show which specific layers/cells most strongly drive the echo behavior,
- try injections on different prompts (not just identity prompts) to test whether the effect generalizes to other contexts,
- or attempt to separate the possible “sensational/headline” cluster from the echo cluster.
